metric_rationale: The experiment is designed to pit Take The Best against Tallying by presenting option pairs where the highest-validity discriminating cue points to one option, but the overall tally of winning cues points to the other. By calculating the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns with the Take The Best prediction (i.e., choosing the option that wins on the first discriminating cue), we establish a metric where the TTB model will score significantly above 0.5, whereas the Tallying model will score significantly below 0.5.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Tallying heuristic's predictions. The experimental design systematically pits Tallying against Take The Best (TTB) on every single trial. Consequently, an agent following Tallying will score close to 1.0 on this metric, whereas an agent following TTB will score close to 0.0. This stark contrast ensures maximal separation between the two theories, with minimal between-subject variance within each theory.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the WADD (Weighted Additive) theory on the specific subset of trials where WADD and Tallying make strictly opposing predictions. For example, when option A has only the single most valid cue and option B has the three less valid cues, WADD strongly prefers A while Tallying strongly prefers B. By isolating these trials, the metric will be close to 1 under WADD and close to 0 under Tallying, providing maximum discrimination.

The experimental design was specifically crafted such that Tallying (which counts raw feature wins) and WADD (which weights features by log-odds validities) strictly disagree on almost all trials. For example, Option A might win on 3 low-validity features while Option B wins on 1 high-validity feature. Tallying will consistently prefer Option A, whereas WADD will prefer Option B. This metric calculates the proportion of trials where the subject's choice aligns with the Tallying heuristic's strict preference. Data simulated under Tallying will yield a high proportion (approaching 1.0 for low noise), whereas data simulated under WADD will yield a very low proportion (approaching 0.0), strongly discriminating the two theories.

Calculates the overall proportion of trials where Option A is chosen. By design, Option A always contains the single highest-validity cue, which dominates under log-odds weighting but is outvoted by the sum of multiple moderate cues under linear weighting. Thus, this proportion will be near 1 for Log-Odds WADD and near 0 for Linear WADD.

By isolating specific trials where a single high-validity cue is pitted against two lower-validity cues, we can perfectly dissociate the two integration models. Linear WADD (which subtracts 0.5 from validities) evaluates the sum of the lower-validity cues as greater than the single high-validity cue, thus favoring the combination. Log-Odds WADD (Bayesian weighting) assigns exponentially more weight to the top validities, thus favoring the single high-validity cue. The metric computes the proportion of choices favoring the single high-validity cue on these critical trials.
